jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer 4 - Finance Tech
jobs.description:
Do you love building and pioneering in the AI and technology space? Do you enjoy solving complex business problems in a fast-paced, collaborative, inclusive, and iterative delivery environment? At Capital One, you'll be part of a big group of makers, breakers, doers and disruptors who love to solve real problems and meet real customer needs. We are seeking Machine Learning Engineers
who are passionate about leveraging cutting-edge open source frameworks, advanced algorithms, and emerging technologies to join our team. As a Machine Learning Engineer, you’ll have the opportunity to be on the forefront of driving major AI transformations and scaling production models across Capital One.

Finance Tech is responsible for transforming Capital One's financial engine into the most trusted, nimble, and insightful in the industry. Our core mission is to engineer outcomes that strategically enable the Finance organization and the broader Enterprise to remain efficient. This mission is driven by four technical and functional pillars: Forecasting & Resiliency, providing advanced decision support; Treasury & Trade managing sophisticated cash and investment lifecycles; and Accounting & Reporting, ensuring the integrity of our general ledger and regulatory commitments. Powering these pillars are our Data and Core capabilities, which manage the orchestration, sourcing, and pipelines for critical financial data products.

By defining the next generation of financial technology, we ensure that every business process is backed by high fidelity tracking and reporting. Together, we are not just supporting the bottom line - we are building a strategic enabler that operates as a world class financial engine.

What You’ll Do:

The MLE role overlaps with many disciplines, such as Ops, Modeling, and Data Engineering. In this role, you'll be expected to perform many ML engineering activities, including one or more of the following:
Design, build, and/or deliver ML models and components that solve real-world business problems, while working in collaboration with the Product and Data Science teams
Inform your ML infrastructure decisions using your understanding of ML modeling techniques and issues, including choice of model, data, and feature selection, model training, hyperparameter tuning, dimensionality, bias/variance, and validation)
Solve complex problems by writing and testing application code, developing and validating ML models, and automating tests and deployment
Collaborate as part of a cross-functional Agile team to create and enhance software that enables state-of-the-art big data and ML applications
Retrain, maintain, and monitor models in production
Leverage or build cloud-based architectures, technologies, and/or platforms to deliver optimized ML models at scale
Construct optimized data pipelines to feed ML models
Leverage continuous integration and continuous deployment best practices, including test automation and monitoring, to ensure successful deployment of ML models and application code
Ensure all code is well-managed to reduce vulnerabilities, models are well-governed from a risk perspective, and the ML follows best practices in Responsible and Explainable AI
Use programming languages like Python, Scala, or Java

This role is designated as a hybrid position. You are expected to adhere to Capital One's hybrid policy regarding required on-site presence at your designated office location.

Basic Qualifications:

Bachelor's Degree or higher in Computer Science, Machine Learning or a related quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Engineering)
At least 4 years of experience programming with Python, Java, Golang, or C++
At least 4 years of Machine Learning experience using industry standard frameworks PyTorch or Tensorflow and libraries (Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn)
At least 4 years of experience using and operating large scale distributed systems (Spark, Ray) to prepare AI or Machine Learning data
At least 2 years of experience deploying and operating Machine Learning solutions in production and operating production services in the cloud (AWS, GCP, Azure) and using Kubernetes to manage large scale containerized Machine Learning software systems

Preferred Qualifications:

Master's or Doctoral Degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, or related field
3+ years of experience optimizing ML algorithms, configurations, and infrastructure
3+ years of experience following software development best practices including source control, testing, code reviews, CI/CD, etc.
3+ years of experience building resilient software solutions with pre-production testing, advanced deployment techniques (one-box, blue/green, gradual dial-up), monitoring, alarms, and preparing incident response plans.
3+ years of experience working with Machine Learning techniques (Supervised, semi-supervised, and unsupervised, reinforcement learning, etc.) model types (Regression, Classification, Clustering, etc.), model Architectures (RNNs, CNNs, LSTMs, Transformers), training concepts (loss function, hyperparameters, regularization), and how to evaluate model accuracy and diagnose and address common issues (underfitting, overfitting)
3+ years of experience designing, implementing, and scaling production-ready data pipelines for training and evaluating ML models.
1+ years of experience as a technical lead developing ML solutions using industry best practices, patterns, and automation
Authored/co-authored a paper on a ML technique, model, or proof of concept

At this time, Capital One will not sponsor a new applicant for employment authorization, or offer any immigration related support for this position (e.g. H1B, F-1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, F-1 CPT, J-1, TN, E-3, and O-1,
or any other forms of work authorization that require immigration support from an employer
).

The minimum and maximum full-time annual salaries for this role are listed below, by location. Please note that this salary information is solely for candidates hired to perform work within one of these locations, and refers to the amount Capital One is willing to pay at the time of this posting. Salaries for part-time roles will be prorated based upon the agreed upon number of hours to be regularly worked.

McLean, VA: $197,300 - $225,100 for Machine Learning Engineer 4

This role is also eligible to earn performance based incentive compensation, which may include cash bonus(es) and/or long term incentives (LTI). Incentives could be discretionary or non discretionary depending on the plan.

At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

Position Summary

CVS Health is hiring a Lead Agentic AI Solutions Engineer to join the AI/ML Solutions Delivery organization and build enterprise-scale agentic AI and intelligent automation solutions. The Lead Agentic AI Solutions Engineer will serve as a full-stack AI engineer, designing, developing, and deploying production-ready applications that combine modern software engineering practices with generative AI and agentic frameworks. This role will lead the engineering and operationalization of enterprise-scale Agentic AI solutions supporting IT Operations, Cybersecurity, and intelligent automation use cases. The individual will architect, develop, and deploy end-to-end production agentic systems leveraging multi-agent architectures, prompt engineering, context engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), GraphRAG, memory frameworks, evaluation pipelines, and AI guardrails. This role will leverage technologies including ServiceNow, Databricks, Google Vertex AI, Azure AI Foundry, Anthropic Claude, Python, APIs, and cloud-native services to deliver secure, scalable, and resilient solutions.

The Lead Agentic AI Solutions Engineer will own the end-to-end development lifecycle, spanning application architecture, backend services, AI orchestration, data integration, deployment, and operational support.

In addition to hands-on engineering responsibilities, this role will serve as a technical leader for assigned initiatives, providing architectural guidance, mentoring junior engineers, interns, and contractors, and helping establish engineering standards and best practices for enterprise AI delivery. Working closely with Architecture, Cybersecurity, Platform Engineering, Product, and Operations teams, this individual will help accelerate enterprise AI adoption while ensuring solutions meet CVS Health standards for security, governance, performance, reliability, and responsible AI practices.

Design and implement end-to-end agentic AI systems utilizing multi-agent architectures, prompt engineering, context engineering, tool orchestration, memory frameworks, AI guardrails, and evaluation frameworks.
Build and optimize Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), GraphRAG, vector search, document ingestion, and enterprise knowledge integration solutions to improve AI accuracy and decision-making.
Lead the full solution lifecycle from architecture and prototyping through production deployment, monitoring, optimization, and continuous improvement while making informed technical tradeoff decisions.
Implement secure-by-design architectures incorporating AI security controls, data privacy protections, prompt injection safeguards, resiliency patterns, failover mechanisms, and responsible AI practices.
Collaborate with Architecture, Cybersecurity, Platform Engineering, Product, and Operations teams while providing technical mentorship to interns and contractor resources, and serving as a technical lead for assigned initiatives.

7+ years developing software, AI/ML, intelligent automation, or full-stack applications with demonstrated ownership of complex enterprise solutions.
5+ years designing scalable cloud-native systems while applying AI governance, security, privacy, access management, resiliency, and operational reliability best practices.
Proven track record delivering production-ready automation, generative AI, or agentic AI solutions beyond proof-of-concept environments, including experience building multi-agent systems, workflow orchestration solutions, or intelligent automation platforms.
3+ years building Python-based applications, APIs, microservices, and cloud-native services utilizing modern software engineering practices, CI/CD pipelines, and automated testing approaches.
Hands-on experience implementing RAG architectures, vector search, document ingestion, LLM integrations, prompt engineering, context engineering, evaluation frameworks, testing harnesses, and agent performance measurement methodologies within enterprise environments.

Experience with agent engineering concepts including prompt engineering, context engineering, AI guardrails, evaluation frameworks, benchmark testing, model observability, and responsible AI controls.

Experience supporting healthcare, pharmacy, insurance, cybersecurity, AIOps, SecOps, or other highly regulated environments, with exposure to Databricks Mosaic AI, Google Agent Development Kit (ADK), Azure AI Foundry, AWS Bedrock, LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, AutoGen, CrewAI, or similar agent orchestration technologies.

Description & Requirements

Who we are

lululemon is an innovative performance apparel company for yoga, running, training, and other athletic pursuits. As a company, we focus on creating positive change to build a healthier, thriving future. In particular, that includes creating an equitable, inclusive and growth-focused environment for our people.

About This Team

The Enterprise Data & AI team is a strategic and operational driver of growth for lululemon, owning and building the data and AI platforms and products that enable the enterprise to operate with intelligence at scale. The team leads the design and delivery of a trusted unified data foundation, advanced analytics capabilities, and AI solutions across lululemon’s vertically integrated retail ecosystem, embedding strong data governance and responsible AI practices from the very beginning. By applying AI to critical business challenges and creating new, transformative AI solutions, the team helps reshape how lululemon operates. Through deep partnership with product, technology, and business teams, Enterprise Data & AI accelerates product innovation, unlocks measurable value, elevates guest and educator experiences, and drives enterprise efficiency.

Core Responsibilities

As an AI/ML Engineer, you will contribute to the design and implementation of AI/ML systems across the full model lifecycle from dataset curation, feature engineering, and model training through evaluation, deployment, and production monitoring. You will contribute to meaningful technical decisions on model architecture, training strategies, and serving infrastructure, working with minimal supervision to deliver reliable, high-quality AI capabilities aligned to business objectives. You will collaborate closely with research scientists, data scientists, and product engineers to translate model innovations into scalable production systems, and begin to develop mentorship and knowledge-sharing habits within the team.

Select Responsibilities Include

Design and implement end-to-end AI/ML systems covering dataset curation, feature engineering, model training, hyperparameter optimization, evaluation, deployment, and retraining
Apply appropriate model architectures, training strategies, and optimization techniques for given tasks including classification, regression, ranking, generation, and retrieval
Build and maintain scalable model training pipelines using distributed training frameworks (PyTorch Distributed, Horovod, Ray Train) and cloud ML platforms (SageMaker, Vertex AI, Azure ML)
Deploy models to production using CI/CD automation including A/B testing, canary rollouts, shadow deployment, and automated rollback procedures
Contribute to implementation of model serving infrastructure meeting latency, throughput, and cost requirements using serving frameworks (TorchServe, Triton, BentoML, or equivalent)

jobs.description:
ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD.

At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future.

Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career.

THE ROLE

AMD is looking for a research engineer with practical implementation experience to advance AI-based medical imaging at the intersection of clinical imaging, deep learning, and high-performance computing on AMD platforms.

You will work across the full medical imaging workflow, from data preparation and preprocessing through model inference, post-processing, and evaluation, investigating modern pipelines and optimizing their design and implementation on AMD platforms. You will build reference designs, GPU kernels, and agentic frameworks that let these pipelines run at maximum performance on AMD devices such as the Ryzen AI Max+ and Radeon AI Pro, with hardware–model co-design as a central theme: tailoring model architecture to the properties of the underlying hardware so that computation maps efficiently onto the device. Areas of interest include image reconstruction, segmentation, detection, classification, tracking, and quality assessment across modalities such as ultrasound, CT, MRI, and X-ray.

Working with AMD engineering and research teams, industry partners, and clinical collaborators, you will take imaging pipelines from problem definition through implementation, optimization, and evaluation; document your methods and results; and feed what you learn back to the libraries and kernel teams. Your findings will help establish the design frameworks and best practices for customers migrating imaging pipelines to AMD devices, and over time steer the team’s roadmap toward the co-design of next-generation imaging models: architected from the outset around AMD hardware for better mapping and efficiency.

THE PERSON

You bring a strong understanding of AI-based medical imaging and the programming skills to turn imaging models and algorithms into efficient software on AMD hardware. You have demonstrated experience writing code, profiling and tuning performance, and solving difficult technical problems. You can distinguish improvements that matter to a clinical imaging workflow running on device from gains in an isolated benchmark and communicate your findings clearly to both domain experts and systems engineers.

We value depth in one or more relevant areas, curiosity across the clinical, algorithmic, and systems disciplines, and the ability to take ownership of a technical project from investigation to validated results.

Key Responsibilities

Analyze modern AI-based medical imaging pipelines, understanding their clinical objectives, algorithms, computational requirements, and practical limitations.
Collaborate with research and industry partners to design and build new AI models for medical imaging.
Build or modify components of medical imaging pipelines across modalities such as ultrasound, CT, MRI, and X-ray.
Prepare, preprocess, and validate imaging data in coordination with the team’s data-handling and privacy procedures.
Integrate and evaluate AI models for tasks such as reconstruction, segmentation, detection, classification, and tracking.
Measure and profile model and pipeline performance against agreed metrics such as latency, throughput, occupancy, and memory use.
Develop agentic frameworks that let domain experts target AMD devices more efficiently at the algorithm and graph-design level.
Develop prototypes, scripts, tests, and technical documentation.
Present findings and recommendations to internal teams, collaborators, and partners.

Required Experience

Strong programming skills in Python and experience with C++ or another language used for high-performance computing.
Hands-on experience implementing machine learning or deep learning models for imaging applications.
Experience with agentic design flows and AI coding tools such as Claude.
Solid understanding of image processing and common medical imaging concepts.
Experience profiling, debugging, and improving computational software.
Ability to make progress independently while on a defined technical problem and collaborate effectively across medical and engineering disciplines.
Clear written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred Experience

Medical imaging modalities such as ultrasound, CT, MRI, or X-ray, in depth.
Imaging libraries and formats such as SimpleITK, ITK, MONAI, OpenCV, DICOM, and NIfTI.
Deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow, including custom operators or distributed training and inference.
Inference deployment and optimization with ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, ROCm, MIGraphX, HIP, CUDA, Triton, or comparable stacks.
Real-time, embedded, or GPU-accelerated pipelines.
GPU profiling and tuning of AI models to target GPU hardware more effectively.
Clinical or regulated data workflows, demonstrated through research, coursework, or projects.

ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS

Master’s or PhD in Biomedical Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Medical Physics, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience preferred.

jobs.title: Life Sciences AI Research Engineer
jobs.description:
ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD.

At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future.

Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career.

THE ROLE

AMD is looking for a hands-on research engineer to advance life sciences computing at the intersection of computational biology, AI, and high-performance computing.

You will investigate emerging scientific workloads, develop and optimize algorithms, and build software that enables researchers to tackle larger and more complex biological problems on AMD platforms. Areas of interest include genomics, biological foundation models, protein and molecular modeling, and computational drug discovery.

Working with AMD researchers, software engineers, and external collaborators, you will take projects from scientific problem definition through implementation and evaluation. Your findings will help identify where AMD can deliver meaningful advances in life sciences computing and guide future research and software investments.

THE PERSON

You bring deep understanding of a computational life sciences domain and the programming skills to turn scientific ideas into working software. You enjoy writing code, testing hypotheses, and solving difficult technical problems. You can distinguish improvements that matter to a scientific workflow from gains in an isolated benchmark and communicate your findings clearly to both domain scientists and systems engineers.

We value depth in one or more relevant areas, curiosity across disciplines, and the ability to take ownership of a technical project from investigation to validated results.

Key Responsibilities

Investigate important and emerging life sciences workloads, understanding their scientific objectives, algorithms, computational requirements, and practical limitations.
Develop, implement, and evaluate algorithms and AI methods for applications in genomics, biomolecular modeling, or related areas.
Profile and optimize scientific applications and AI workflows on AMD platforms, addressing bottlenecks in computation, memory, data processing, and communication.
Explore algorithmic reformulations, parallelization strategies, numerical precision, and GPU acceleration while preserving scientific validity.
Build reproducible benchmarks that measure end-to-end performance, scalability, resource use, and relevant scientific outcomes.
Work directly with academic and industry collaborators to translate scientific needs into technical requirements and working implementations.
Contribute reusable software, optimized operators, and improvements to relevant open-source projects.
Translate experimental findings into recommendations for AMD’s research priorities, software capabilities, and hardware requirements.
Communicate results through technical reports, demonstrations, publications, and invention disclosures, as appropriate.

Required Experience

Strong computational expertise in at least one life sciences area, such as computational genomics, bioinformatics, protein modeling, computational chemistry, or molecular simulation.
Hands-on experience implementing scientific algorithms or developing machine learning models for biological applications.
Strong programming skills in Python and experience with C++ or another language used for high-performance scientific computing.
Solid understanding of algorithms, data structures, numerical methods, and experimental evaluation.
Experience profiling, debugging, and improving computational software.
Ability to work independently on a defined technical problem and collaborate effectively across scientific and engineering disciplines.
Clear written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred Experience

Biological foundation models, protein structure prediction or design, molecular generative models, or genomic sequence modeling.
Scientific AI architectures, including transformers, geometric deep learning, graph neural networks, or diffusion models.
GPU programming and optimization using HIP, CUDA, Triton, or comparable technologies.
Deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch, including custom operators or distributed training and inference.
Parallel algorithms, multi-GPU computing, or large-scale scientific workflows.
Established life sciences software ecosystems and experience extending or contributing to open-source tools.
Research contributions demonstrated through publications, software, patents, or deployed scientific applications.

ACADEMIC CREDENTIALS

Master’s, or PhD in Computational Biology, Bioinformatics, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Computational Chemistry, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience preferred.

LOCATION:
Longmont, CO; Austin, TX and Santa Clara, Ca are options.

This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

jobs.title: Senior Staff Software Engineer, AI-Native Engineering - Flow
jobs.description:
Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

About Team

Flow by ServiceNow is a standalone conversational AI service desk, with its own product and its own codebase. Employees ask for help wherever they already work — Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, or the browser. Flow answers from connected knowledge, handles the request, and runs automations the team publishes. AI is how the product works, and a person stays in control when the action is sensitive.

Flow is a new company inside ServiceNow, reimagining every function from first principles. We hire builders with agency and curiosity who use AI as the default way to design, review, and operate. They challenge inherited ways of working and treat their work as craft.

On AI-Native Engineering, you’ll set technical direction for the systems that make Flow intelligent: the agent runtime, the tool surface a model sees, the prompt and context layers, the retrieval that grounds every answer, and the evaluation discipline that tells us whether a change made the product better. This is a hands-on role with broad influence — you’ll make architectural calls, raise the engineering bar, and help the team move from AI-assisted development to AI-native delivery.

What You’ll Do

Lead the design and delivery of complex, cross-functional features across the product, from architecture through production operations.
Build AI-native capabilities: agent loops and the tools they call, prompt and context design, retrieval that grounds and cites its answers, and the eval harnesses that tell us whether a change actually made the product better — with reliability and governance built in.
Define and drive how the team uses AI across the development lifecycle: code generation, test automation, review, triage, and documentation. Agentic coding is central to how this team ships. Measure the impact and share what works.
Mentor senior and mid-level engineers and set standards for code quality, observability, and safe AI usage.
Partner with product, UX, and other engineering leads to turn ambiguous problems into scoped, shippable plans.
Own production quality for your area, including defect triage, release readiness, and gate reviews.

Qualifications

What we’re looking for

We don’t expect anyone to match every line below. Depth matters more to us than a match on any particular toolchain — be excellent in a modern typed stack and quick to pick up a new one.

Experience leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This includes current, hands-on fluency with AI-assisted and agentic development, and an opinion on where those tools help and where they don’t.
12+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of technical leadership at the staff level or equivalent.
Strong proficiency in TypeScript or another statically typed language, plus solid system design skills.
Hands-on experience building or integrating LLM-based features: prompt design, retrieval or context management, evaluation, and cost/latency tradeoffs.
Working knowledge of agentic architectures, including tool use, orchestration, and human-in-the-loop controls.
Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to brief senior leaders and align multiple teams.
Familiarity with enterprise SaaS, multi-tenant systems, and secure, compliant software delivery.

Why this role matters

The agent runtime is the product. The patterns you set — how an agent decides, which tools it may call, what it must prove before it acts, and how we measure whether it got better — are what customers experience as intelligent workflows.

For positions in this location, we offer a base pay of $171,900 - $300,800
, plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. Sales positions generally offer a competitive On Target Earnings (OTE) incentive compensation structure. Please note that the base pay shown is a guideline, and individual total compensation will vary based on factors such as qualifications, skill level, competencies, and work location. We also offer health plans, including flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) Plan with company match, ESPP, matching donations, a flexible time away plan and family leave programs. Compensation is based on the geographic location in which the role is located and is subject to change based on work location.

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

About Team

Flow by ServiceNow is a standalone conversational AI service desk, with its own product and its own codebase. Employees ask for help wherever they already work — Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, or the browser. Flow answers from connected knowledge, handles the request, and runs automations the team publishes. AI is how the product works, and a person stays in control when the action is sensitive.

Flow is a new company inside ServiceNow, reimagining every function from first principles. We hire builders with agency and curiosity who use AI as the default way to design, review, and operate. They challenge inherited ways of working and treat their work as craft.

On AI-Native Engineering, you’ll set technical direction for the systems that make Flow intelligent: the agent runtime, the tool surface a model sees, the prompt and context layers, the retrieval that grounds every answer, and the evaluation discipline that tells us whether a change made the product better. This is a hands-on role with broad influence — you’ll make architectural calls, raise the engineering bar, and help the team move from AI-assisted development to AI-native delivery.

What You’ll Do

Lead the design and delivery of complex, cross-functional features across the product, from architecture through production operations.
Build AI-native capabilities: agent loops and the tools they call, prompt and context design, retrieval that grounds and cites its answers, and the eval harnesses that tell us whether a change actually made the product better — with reliability and governance built in.
Define and drive how the team uses AI across the development lifecycle: code generation, test automation, review, triage, and documentation. Agentic coding is central to how this team ships. Measure the impact and share what works.
Mentor senior and mid-level engineers and set standards for code quality, observability, and safe AI usage.
Partner with product, UX, and other engineering leads to turn ambiguous problems into scoped, shippable plans.

We don’t expect anyone to match every line below. Depth matters more to us than a match on any particular toolchain — be excellent in a modern typed stack and quick to pick up a new one.

Experience leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This includes current, hands-on fluency with AI-assisted and agentic development, and an opinion on where those tools help and where they don’t.
8+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of technical leadership at the staff level or equivalent.
Strong proficiency in TypeScript or another statically typed language, plus solid system design skills.
Hands-on experience building or integrating LLM-based features: prompt design, retrieval or context management, evaluation, and cost/latency tradeoffs.

Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to brief senior leaders and align multiple teams.

The agent runtime is the product. The patterns you set — how an agent decides, which tools it may call, what it must prove before it acts, and how we measure whether it got better — are what customers experience as intelligent workflows.

jobs.description:
Location: Indianapolis, IN

Position Summary

The Solutions Architect - AI
owns the technical design of how enterprise business knowledge is captured, structured, and served to AI systems, so they answer business questions accurately. The role designs the domain context model, the context repository, and the evaluation harness that measures AI accuracy before and after context is added. It also designs the agentic automation and playbook that letst RADcube onboard new data domains faster than the first. The architect sets technical direction for a team that includes a techno-functional architect, a data and AI engineer, a validation engineer, and a business analyst, and presents progress to client sponsors every week.

Key Responsibilities

Context Architecture and Domain Modeling

Define the Domain Context Model: the context elements and minimum standards that make a data product "context complete."
Design the domain ontology (business concepts, relationships, hierarchies, synonyms) and map it to data products and the client's knowledge graph and semantic layer.
Run a rapid baseline of existing metadata, definitions, and data classification (PII, GxP-regulated, internal, public), and close gaps that block business context.
Set up ontology ownership, review, and change processes so context stays current as the business changes.

Business Context Repository and Integration

Architect the Business Context Repository in a client-approved environment, starting simple and hardening it to client security and data standards.
Integrate the repository with the client's context injection layer, metadata registry, catalogs, and graph, without rebuilding components the client already owns.
Align access controls to dataset classification.
Deliver source code, configuration, and runbooks to the client repository.

AI Evaluation and Accuracy

Design the evaluation harness: ground-truth question and answer sets, an evaluation runner that tests AI answers with and without domain context, and grading by numeric match, query-result comparison, and rubric.
Build the failure-mode taxonomy (hallucination, stale data, misread schema, wrong join or aggregation, missing business context, persona mismatch) and the scoring rubric.
Use Claude or another approved LLM to generate and score answers, then iterate on context and re-test to measure improvement.
Report before and after accuracy by dataset, question type, and failure mode, and rate each data product as AI-ready or not, with remediation.

Agentic Automation and Scale

Design agentic workflows, orchestration patterns, and human-in-the-loop controls that draft, review, and refresh context at scale.
Automate intake from existing sources (metadata registry, catalogs, workshop outputs, BI reports, usage logs) and feedback loops from the questions users ask.
Build scheduled refresh and staleness flags so context does not drift.
Author the domain onboarding playbook, effort model, and prioritized roadmap for onboarding additional domains across a large data estate.

Client Leadership and Knowledge Transfer

Serve as the technical lead with client program leads, data owners, and sponsors; confirm scope, success criteria, and priorities.
Lead weekly demonstrations and incremental releases aligned to the client's release calendar.
Guide business analysts in turning ambiguous business asks into structured, testable questions.
Run knowledge transfer sessions and produce handover documentation.

Requirements

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in computer science, Data Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
8+ years in data architecture or solutions architecture, including 3+ years designing AI or LLM solutions for production use.

jobs.description:
Description

Software Engineer – AI, Autonomy & Platform Development

Overview

The Leidos Office of Technology is seeking Software Engineers with AI and autonomy experience to help build a common technology platform.

In this role, you will design, build, and operate production software for AI-driven and autonomous systems. You will work in small, accountable build-and-run teams, using modern AI-assisted development practices to ship faster and at higher quality. Your work will support national security and other critical missions where reliability, security, and human oversight matter.

Location:
The ideal candidate will be based in Northern Virginia or near another Leidos facility, such as Huntsville, AL, or San Diego, CA. Onsite work at a Leidos facility is required as business needs dictate.

What You’ll Do

Design and build AI agents and reasoning services, including LLM-based agents, planning, and inference, with human oversight, auditability, and fail-safe behavior built in.
Develop autonomy software and integrate it with sensors, platforms, and hardware across edge and cloud environments.
Design and develop platform software, including APIs and SDKs, data and knowledge services, and user-facing applications.
Package components as reusable, secure, well-documented assets that others can adopt without rework.
Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and release evidence (SBOM, provenance, signing) that support secure release and deployment.
Own what you build in production, including observability, reliability, and incident response.
Contribute to engineering standards, reusable patterns, and technical-debt reduction across the platform.
Collaborate with program teams and architects to turn customer needs into repeatable capabilities.
Use AI-assisted development tools (coding assistants, agentic workflows, automated review and test generation) in daily engineering, and help teams adopt them effectively and responsibly.
Help evaluate emerging AI, autonomy, and developer-productivity technologies, and scale what works.

Basic Qualifications

We are hiring software engineers at all levels, from junior through senior, with opportunities tailored to individual experience and expertise in AI-enabled software development.
At the early career level, the ideal candidate would have a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, combined with 4+ years of experience. (Additional years of experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.)
At the mid level, the ideal candidate would have a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, combined with 8+ years of experience. (Additional years of experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.)
At the senior level, the ideal candidate would have a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, combined with 12+ years of experience. (Additional years of experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.)
Hands-on software development experience in one or more modern languages such as Python, C++, Rust, Java, Go, or TypeScript.
Experience (professional, academic, or personal projects) building AI/ML-enabled or autonomous systems, such as LLM agents, robotics, perception, planning, or sensor-driven software.
Working knowledge of Git-based workflows, CI/CD, automated testing, and DevSecOps practices.
Experience using AI-assisted development tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, or comparable) and the ability to quickly adopt new tools.
Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively in small, cross-functional teams.
U.S. citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience building AI/ML-enabled systems, including LLM agents, agent frameworks, evaluation harnesses, or retrieval and data pipelines.
Experience with autonomy or robotics software, including perception, planning, control, sensor fusion, simulation, ROS 2, or DDS.
Experience with edge and embedded systems, real-time or deterministic software, Linux and real-time operating systems, or GPU/accelerator programming.
Experience designing APIs, SDKs, or developer platforms, including extensible component architectures, developer experience, platform engineering, or software modernization.
Experience with cloud and container technologies (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud; Docker, Kubernetes) and infrastructure as code.
Familiarity with secure software supply chain practices, static analysis, and security scanning tools (e.g., SonarQube, Fortify, Checkmarx).
Understanding of responsible AI practices for assured autonomy, including human-in-the-loop control, audit trails, and IP and data-handling considerations in AI-assisted development.
Background supporting federal, defense, intelligence, or homeland security missions, and an active Top Secret clearance.

If you're looking for comfort, keep scrolling. At Leidos, we outthink, outbuild, and outpace the status quo — because the mission demands it. We're not hiring followers. We're recruiting the ones who disrupt, provoke, and refuse to fail. Step 10 is ancient history. We're already at step 30 — and moving faster than anyone else dares.

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.description:
About Valence

Valence is the AI company behind Nadia, a personalized coach for everyone that advances talent strategy at enterprise scale. Valence’s talent system connects context on individuals, the organization, and the work to embed personalized, proactive development into the day-to-day. Employees build new skills and behaviors, teams work better together, and HR leaders extend the reach and impact of their talent programs, with measurable gains in learning, culture, and performance.

Since launching in early 2023, Nadia has supported millions of coaching conversations in 100+ languages at leading global enterprises, including Delta Air Lines, Coca-Cola, IBM, Schneider Electric, CVS Health, Merck, Kraft Heinz, Telefónica, Prudential, and General Mills. Valence is a Series B company backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and Insight Partners, with offices in New York, Toronto, London, and San Francisco. Learn more at valence.co.

Learn more about our work with Microsoft: Valence Brings AI Coaching More Deeply Into the Flow of Work with Microsoft 365

At Valence, our team is focused on problems that actually decide whether AI changes how organizations operate — the ones with no playbook, no obvious answers, and no guarantee of success. If you want to be part of the small group that defines how AI transforms the future at a global scale, this is your chance.

And this isn’t for everyone. We’re not looking for people who want predictability or incremental progress. We only want those who are restless at the edge of what’s possible, who get bored when things feel “done,” and who are driven to redefine what AI can mean for leaders, companies, and the world. Because at Valence, the work worth doing is the kind that redefines work itself.

The Role

Nadia lives where people already work and connects to the systems that run talent at our customers, such as Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, data lakes and learning platforms. Our customers are some of the largest employers in the world, and each one runs a slightly different stack.

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you build customer implementations inside a customer's real environment, using our standard pipes and custom integrations. Once a deal is signed, you take the scope our Sales Engineers wrote and turn it into working integrations. You pull a customer's data out of systems we haven't connected to before, map it cleanly into Nadia and run it in production. You work directly with customer engineers and IT and ship in weeks.

You build what was scoped, and you speak up early when the scope is wrong. When a customer asks for a quick addition, you know it belongs back with the account team. When a one-off keeps coming up, you know it should become a reusable connector.

Our CHRO clients are bringing Nadia deeper into their own technology, including their performance data, talent systems and internal tools. Sales Engineering now scopes that work before signature. We are hiring our founding Forward Deployed Engineers to deliver it, run it, and turn it into the connectors every future customer gets as standard. You will sit in Engineering and work day to day with the account teams on your accounts.

What You'll Do

Build and ship custom integrations on top of Nadia's standard pipes, connecting new data sources (ServiceNow, Snowflake, custom data lakes, internal APIs, SFTP feeds) to Nadia's context layer.
Work hands-on with customers' engineers, data owners and IT to get access, agree field mappings and test against real data.
Own data quality end to end, including identity matching, unit and definition drift, duplicates, late and restated data, terminations and deletions.
Build privacy and works-council commitments into the code itself with allowlisted fields, per-country rules, least-privilege access and clean deletion.
Run what you ship. Set up monitoring and alerting, handle incidents, and hand over runbooks so Support can operate it.
Use AI every day. That means coding agents to build faster, and your LLM knowledge to shape how customer data grounds Nadia's coaching and how we test that it helps.
Work with core Engineering to turn repeated custom work into reusable connectors and libraries, so the next customer's setup is standard.
Spot expansion. When a customer's data or workflows point to the next use case, bring it to the account team with a clear technical picture.

What We're Looking For

4+ years as a software engineer, including 2+ years building integrations or data pipelines that customers depended on in production.
Strong Python or TypeScript skills. You write clean, tested code you would be happy for someone else to maintain.
Hands-on experience with enterprise integration patterns: REST and SOAP APIs, pagination and rate limits, OAuth and service accounts, SFTP and batch file feeds, webhooks, incremental sync and idempotency.
Good data modeling instincts. You can look at a messy export and spot the identity, unit and duplicate problems before they reach production.
Experience working directly with customers' technical teams, including telling them kindly when something is out of scope and routing it to the right person.
Production habits such as logging without leaking sensitive data, retries with backoff, alerting and runbooks.
AI fluency. You use coding agents every day, and you can explain how an LLM product is given context, grounded and evaluated, and where it fails.
A privacy and security mindset. You treat employee data as sensitive and know what least privilege, data minimization and data residency mean in code.

Nice to Have

Experience with Workday, ServiceNow, Snowflake or Databricks APIs and data models.
Experience with Microsoft Azure, Teams apps or the Microsoft 365 ecosystem.
Experience building eval sets or quality checks for LLM features.
Experience as a forward deployed, solutions or implementation engineer at a growth-stage company.
Experience with EU employee-data requirements such as GDPR or works agreements.

What You'll Get

Ownership & Rapid Growth
Outsized missions from day one, with direct responsibility for company-defining projects
Work alongside the executive team with transparency into strategy and decision-making
Influence on direction through real-time customer feedback and market insights
AI-First Operator
Work directly with cutting-edge AI models and next-generation platforms
Build expertise in enterprise AI implementation across Fortune 500 companies and multiple industries
Establish yourself as a recognized leader among peers in shaping how AI transforms work at a global scale
Compensation
Competitive salary including base + bonuses
Comprehensive health coverage (medical, dental, vision) from day one
Generous PTO, company-wide R&R shutdowns, and paid parental leave
Retirement plan support for US and global employees
Equity
Meaningful ownership in a venture-backed company at a growth inflection point
Financial upside that comes from scaling fast
Top-up grants as we scale and you deliver exceptional performance — your compensation grows alongside your impact
Top-Performing Culture
A culture built for top talent: intensity to win, growth without limits, and a team that solves hard problems and celebrates big wins together

Location and Work Environment

This role is remote in the US. Being able to work from our New York office is a plus.

Employment Verification & Commitment

We use third-party services to verify employment history, education, and other information relevant to your candidacy. Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of these verification checks. This is a full-time role that requires a high level of focus, availability, and commitment. Employees may not hold concurrent full-time employment with another organization while employed at Valence. Any outside consulting, advisory, freelance, or other professional work must be disclosed and approved in advance and must not interfere with job responsibilities, availability, performance, or create a conflict of interest - including risks related to confidentiality, intellectual property, or competition.

Diversity and Inclusion

We are dedicated to creating a diverse and inclusive environment where everyone feels valued and supported. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds and offer accommodations upon request throughout the hiring process. Questions can be directed to Allison Langille, Head of People, at jobs@valence.co.

Valence takes candidate fraud seriously. We verify identity, LinkedIn profiles, employment history, and references; any misrepresentation during the hiring process is grounds for withdrawing an offer or ending employment. All offers are contingent on successful completion of these checks.

The Leidos Office of Technology is seeking Software Engineers with AI and autonomy experience to help build a common technology platform.

You will work in small, accountable build-and-run teams, using modern AI-assisted development practices to ship faster and at higher quality. Location:
The ideal candidate will be based in Northern Virginia or near another Leidos facility, such as Huntsville, AL, or San Diego, CA. Onsite work at a Leidos facility is required as business needs dictate.

Design and build AI agents and reasoning services, including LLM-based agents, planning, and inference, with human oversight, auditability, and fail-safe behavior built in.
Develop autonomy software and integrate it with sensors, platforms, and hardware across edge and cloud environments.

Help evaluate emerging AI, autonomy, and developer-productivity technologies, and scale what works.

Agentic capabilities move from prototype to mission use quickly, with working agents integrated into real government workflows rather than remaining isolated demos.

jobs.description:
As an Applied AI Site Reliability Engineer III , you will actively engage in your engineering craft, taking a hands-on approach to the reliability, performance, and operational integrity of high-visibility products and platforms and the environments they run in. Your expertise will be pivotal in keeping production safe, performant, and cost-effective, while driving tangible value for Deloitte's engineering investments. You will leverage your extensive engineering craftsmanship across cloud platform engineering, observability, and performance and reliability engineering-together with applied AI fluency that lets you reliably operate AI and agentic workloads alongside the rest of the portfolio-consistently demonstrating your strong track record in operating high-quality, resilient systems at scale. The ideal candidate will be a dependable team player, collaborating with cross-functional teams to uphold production standards, safeguard environments, and admit systems into production with confidence.

Work You'll Do
:

Outcome-Driven Accountability: Embrace and drive a culture of accountability for reliability, performance, and cost outcomes, measured in service-level objectives and error budgets, not raw uptime. Operate the products, platforms, and environments you support to meet their SLOs within budget, and track incident trends and toil to prioritize the work that most improves reliability-ensuring high-quality, lean operational designs that keep production safe and resilient.
Technical Leadership and Advocacy: Serve as the technical advocate for production reliability and operability, ensuring systems are admissible, performant, safe to run, and able to degrade gracefully when failure occurs. Uphold production standards, lead the design of observability, performance and resilience testing, and operational tooling, and own the admission of systems into production-gating release on error budgets and automated reliability checks, and owning the readiness verification, environment integrity, and operational support that follow.
Engineering Craftsmanship: Maintain accountability for the operational integrity of production and pre-production environments, and for the production standards that systems are admitted against. Own SLOs and error budgets; build and operate production observability-codified, version-controlled dashboards and SLO-driven, actionable alerting that detects before impact, plus the feedback loop into engineering; run performance, ambient-noise, and chaos testing to verify readiness; and guard environments against drift. Stay hands-on, self-driven, and continuously learn new approaches, languages, and frameworks-operating as an infrastructure-focused engineer, not a tool operator. Create technical specifications, runbooks, and shared playbooks; lead blameless postmortems that turn incidents into learning and systemic fixes; write high-quality, supportable automation to ensure all reliability KPIs (availability, performance, and cost) are met or exceeded. Demonstrate collaborative skills to work effectively with diverse teams.
Customer-Centric Engineering: Develop lean operational solutions through rapid, inexpensive experimentation to meet the reliability needs of the engineering teams and the business. Engage with those teams before, during, and after delivery, co-defining service-level objectives and operational readiness so the right safeguards are in place at the right time, without becoming a bottleneck to delivery.
Incremental and Iterative Delivery: Adopt a mindset that favors action and evidence over extensive planning. Utilize a leaning-forward approach to navigate complexity and uncertainty, hardening reliability through incremental, measurable improvements-progressive resilience testing and SLO refinement-rather than big-bang interventions, and keeping operations supportable and maintainable.
Cross-Functional Collaboration and Integration: Work collaboratively with empowered, cross-functional partners: engineering, platform engineering, security and risk, data governance, and engineering leadership and architecture. Uphold production standards and integrate their constraints so that the reliable, performant, and compliant path is the operative path. Co-define service-level objectives with the teams you support, verify readiness, and own the admission decision into production-holding the segregation-of-duties line as a dedicated, embedded function while partnering with security and risk on the control objectives you enforce. Foster a collaborative environment that enhances team synergy and innovation.
Advanced Technical Proficiency: Possess expertise in site reliability and modern production engineering-cloud platform ownership, observability (metrics, tracing, logging), performance and capacity engineering, chaos engineering, and cloud/AI cost engineering-together with applied AI fluency to operate AI and agentic workloads reliably, including AI and Agentic SSDLC, delivering production operations with full automation from discovery to production to operations and all quality checks through the SSDLC lifecycle. Strive to be a role model, leveraging these techniques to optimize reliability, performance, and operational delivery. Demonstrate strong understanding of the full lifecycle of platform and product development, focusing on continuous improvement and learning.
Domain Expertise: Quickly acquire domain knowledge of the products and platforms you operate-and, where they are AI-infused, their distinct production failure modes such as drift, train/serve skew, latency and output variance, and token/GPU cost anomalies. Translate reliability needs, reference architectures, and operational requirements into service-level objectives, runbooks, and production tooling. Be a valuable, flexible, and dedicated team member, supportive of teammates, and focused on quality and tech debt payoff.
Effective Communication and Influence: Exhibit exceptional communication skills, capable of articulating complex technical concepts clearly and compellingly. Inspire and influence teammates and product teams through well-structured arguments and trade-offs supported by evidence. Create coherent narratives that align technical solutions with business objectives.
Engagement and Collaborative Co-Creation: Engage and collaborate with product engineering teams at all organizational levels, including customers as needed. Build and maintain constructive relationships, fostering a culture of co-creation and shared momentum towards achieving product goals. Align diverse perspectives and drive consensus to create feasible solutions.

The team:
US Deloitte Technology Product Engineering has modernized software and product delivery, creating a scalable, cost-effective model that focuses on value/outcomes that leverages a progressive and responsive talent structure. As Deloitte's primary internal development team, Product Engineering delivers innovative digital solutions to businesses, service lines, and internal operations with proven bottom-line results and outcomes. It helps power Deloitte's success. It is the engine that drives Deloitte, serving many of the world's largest, most respected companies. We develop and deploy cutting-edge internal and go-to-market solutions that help Deloitte operate effectively and lead in the market. Our reputation is built on a tradition of delivering with excellence.

The successful candidate will possess:

Excellent interpersonal and organizational skills, with the ability to handle diverse situations, complex projects, and changing priorities, behaving with passion, empathy, and care.

Qualifications

Required:

A bachelor's degree in computer science, software engineering, data science, machine learning, or related discipline. Experience is the most relevant factor.
5+ years of software engineering and site reliability engineering experience operating large-scale, distributed, cloud-native systems in production, with experience in most of the following: Python, Go, Bash, Java, C#/.NET, SQL/NoSQL, Kubernetes, Terraform, ArgoCD, as well as CI/CD and observability stacks.
3+ years of experience in site reliability or production engineering for large-scale systems-defining and owning SLIs, SLOs, and SLAs; error budgets; incident command and on-call; building and operating production observability (metrics, tracing, logging-e.g., OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, Dynatrace, Amazon CloudWatch, Azure Monitor, Google Cloud Operations, SolarWinds, Splunk); environment integrity and drift prevention across pre-production and production; and segregation-of-duties controls (least-privilege/RBAC, deploy approvals, secrets management) in partnership with security and risk.
3+ years of experience with cloud-native engineering and cloud platform ownership on any of the cloud hyperscalers such as Azure, AWS, or GCP-including their AI/ML services such as Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, or Vertex AI-plus container orchestration (Kubernetes, Docker), infrastructure-as-code, networking, and multi-environment management.
Prior experience operating AI/ML and agentic workloads in production-their reliability failure modes (drift, train/serve skew, output variance), MLOps/LLMOps, and the AI control plane (model/LLM gateway, guardrails) from the operability and performance side.
Prior experience with load and performance testing under simulated production traffic (e.g., LoadRunner, k6, or JMeter), chaos engineering (e.g., Azure Chaos Studio, AWS Fault Injector), capacity planning, autoscaling, and cloud/AI cost engineering (FinOps tooling/dashboards, including GPU/inference and token cost attribution).

jobs.title: Applied AI SRE III - PxE GPS
jobs.description:
As an Applied AI Site Reliability Engineer III , you will actively engage in your engineering craft, taking a hands-on approach to the reliability, performance, and operational integrity of high-visibility products and platforms and the environments they run in. Your expertise will be pivotal in keeping production safe, performant, and cost-effective, while driving tangible value for Deloitte's engineering investments. You will leverage your extensive engineering craftsmanship across cloud platform engineering, observability, and performance and reliability engineering-together with applied AI fluency that lets you reliably operate AI and agentic workloads alongside the rest of the portfolio-consistently demonstrating your strong track record in operating high-quality, resilient systems at scale. The ideal candidate will be a dependable team player, collaborating with cross-functional teams to uphold production standards, safeguard environments, and admit systems into production with confidence.

Work You'll Do
:

Outcome-Driven Accountability: Embrace and drive a culture of accountability for reliability, performance, and cost outcomes, measured in service-level objectives and error budgets, not raw uptime. Operate the products, platforms, and environments you support to meet their SLOs within budget, and track incident trends and toil to prioritize the work that most improves reliability-ensuring high-quality, lean operational designs that keep production safe and resilient.
Technical Leadership and Advocacy: Serve as the technical advocate for production reliability and operability, ensuring systems are admissible, performant, safe to run, and able to degrade gracefully when failure occurs. Uphold production standards, lead the design of observability, performance and resilience testing, and operational tooling, and own the admission of systems into production-gating release on error budgets and automated reliability checks, and owning the readiness verification, environment integrity, and operational support that follow.
Engineering Craftsmanship: Maintain accountability for the operational integrity of production and pre-production environments, and for the production standards that systems are admitted against. Own SLOs and error budgets; build and operate production observability-codified, version-controlled dashboards and SLO-driven, actionable alerting that detects before impact, plus the feedback loop into engineering; run performance, ambient-noise, and chaos testing to verify readiness; and guard environments against drift. Stay hands-on, self-driven, and continuously learn new approaches, languages, and frameworks-operating as an infrastructure-focused engineer, not a tool operator. Create technical specifications, runbooks, and shared playbooks; lead blameless postmortems that turn incidents into learning and systemic fixes; write high-quality, supportable automation to ensure all reliability KPIs (availability, performance, and cost) are met or exceeded. Demonstrate collaborative skills to work effectively with diverse teams.
Customer-Centric Engineering: Develop lean operational solutions through rapid, inexpensive experimentation to meet the reliability needs of the engineering teams and the business. Engage with those teams before, during, and after delivery, co-defining service-level objectives and operational readiness so the right safeguards are in place at the right time, without becoming a bottleneck to delivery.
Incremental and Iterative Delivery: Adopt a mindset that favors action and evidence over extensive planning. Utilize a leaning-forward approach to navigate complexity and uncertainty, hardening reliability through incremental, measurable improvements-progressive resilience testing and SLO refinement-rather than big-bang interventions, and keeping operations supportable and maintainable.
Cross-Functional Collaboration and Integration: Work collaboratively with empowered, cross-functional partners: engineering, platform engineering, security and risk, data governance, and engineering leadership and architecture. Uphold production standards and integrate their constraints so that the reliable, performant, and compliant path is the operative path. Co-define service-level objectives with the teams you support, verify readiness, and own the admission decision into production-holding the segregation-of-duties line as a dedicated, embedded function while partnering with security and risk on the control objectives you enforce. Foster a collaborative environment that enhances team synergy and innovation.
Advanced Technical Proficiency: Possess expertise in site reliability and modern production engineering-cloud platform ownership, observability (metrics, tracing, logging), performance and capacity engineering, chaos engineering, and cloud/AI cost engineering-together with applied AI fluency to operate AI and agentic workloads reliably, including AI and Agentic SSDLC, delivering production operations with full automation from discovery to production to operations and all quality checks through the SSDLC lifecycle. Strive to be a role model, leveraging these techniques to optimize reliability, performance, and operational delivery. Demonstrate strong understanding of the full lifecycle of platform and product development, focusing on continuous improvement and learning.
Domain Expertise: Quickly acquire domain knowledge of the products and platforms you operate-and, where they are AI-infused, their distinct production failure modes such as drift, train/serve skew, latency and output variance, and token/GPU cost anomalies. Translate reliability needs, reference architectures, and operational requirements into service-level objectives, runbooks, and production tooling. Be a valuable, flexible, and dedicated team member, supportive of teammates, and focused on quality and tech debt payoff.
Effective Communication and Influence: Exhibit exceptional communication skills, capable of articulating complex technical concepts clearly and compellingly. Inspire and influence teammates and product teams through well-structured arguments and trade-offs supported by evidence. Create coherent narratives that align technical solutions with business objectives.
Engagement and Collaborative Co-Creation: Engage and collaborate with product engineering teams at all organizational levels, including customers as needed. Build and maintain constructive relationships, fostering a culture of co-creation and shared momentum towards achieving product goals. Align diverse perspectives and drive consensus to create feasible solutions.

The team:
US Deloitte Technology Product Engineering has modernized software and product delivery, creating a scalable, cost-effective model that focuses on value/outcomes that leverages a progressive and responsive talent structure. As Deloitte's primary internal development team, Product Engineering delivers innovative digital solutions to businesses, service lines, and internal operations with proven bottom-line results and outcomes. It helps power Deloitte's success. It is the engine that drives Deloitte, serving many of the world's largest, most respected companies. We develop and deploy cutting-edge internal and go-to-market solutions that help Deloitte operate effectively and lead in the market. Our reputation is built on a tradition of delivering with excellence.

The successful candidate will possess:

Excellent interpersonal and organizational skills, with the ability to handle diverse situations, complex projects, and changing priorities, behaving with passion, empathy, and care.

Qualifications

Required:

A bachelor's degree in computer science, software engineering, data science, machine learning, or related discipline. Experience is the most relevant factor.
5+ years of software engineering and site reliability engineering experience operating large-scale, distributed, cloud-native systems in production, with experience in most of the following: Python, Go, Bash, Java, C#/.NET, SQL/NoSQL, Kubernetes, Terraform, ArgoCD, as well as CI/CD and observability stacks.
3+ years of experience in site reliability or production engineering for large-scale systems-defining and owning SLIs, SLOs, and SLAs; error budgets; incident command and on-call; building and operating production observability (metrics, tracing, logging-e.g., OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, Dynatrace, Amazon CloudWatch, Azure Monitor, Google Cloud Operations, SolarWinds, Splunk); environment integrity and drift prevention across pre-production and production; and segregation-of-duties controls (least-privilege/RBAC, deploy approvals, secrets management) in partnership with security and risk.
3+ years of experience with cloud-native engineering and cloud platform ownership on any of the cloud hyperscalers such as Azure, AWS, or GCP-including their AI/ML services such as Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, or Vertex AI-plus container orchestration (Kubernetes, Docker), infrastructure-as-code, networking, and multi-environment management.
Prior experience operating AI/ML and agentic workloads in production-their reliability failure modes (drift, train/serve skew, output variance), MLOps/LLMOps, and the AI control plane (model/LLM gateway, guardrails) from the operability and performance side.
Prior experience with load and performance testing under simulated production traffic (e.g., LoadRunner, k6, or JMeter), chaos engineering (e.g., Azure Chaos Studio, AWS Fault Injector), capacity planning, autoscaling, and cloud/AI cost engineering (FinOps tooling/dashboards, including GPU/inference and token cost attribution).
Prior software engineering experience with the understanding of Business Context Diagrams (BCD), sequence/activity/state/entity relationship/data flow diagrams, OOP/OOD, data structures, algorithms, and code instrumentations, and AI-augmented spec-driven development.
Prior experience using methodologies & tools such as XP, Lean, DevSecOps, SRE, ADO, GitHub, SonarQube, MLflow, and agentic AI frameworks (e.g. LangFuse, LangSmith, or equivalent multi-agent orchestration tools) etc. to operate high-quality, resilient platforms and products at scale.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, AI Compute Scheduling
jobs.description:
NVIDIA is a pioneer in accelerated computing, known for inventing the GPU and driving breakthroughs in gaming, computer graphics, high-performance computing, and artificial intelligence. Our technology powers everything from generative AI to autonomous systems, and we continue to shape the future of computing through innovation and collaboration. Within this mission, our team, Managed AI Research Superclusters (MARS), builds and scales the infrastructure, platforms, and tools that enable researchers and engineers to develop the next generation of AI/ML systems. By joining us, you'll help design solutions that power some of the world's most advanced computing workloads.

The MARS Scheduling team decides how NVIDIA's AI research compute gets used. That fleet spans many of the largest GPU clusters in the world, across multiple clouds and partners, running everything from frontier-model pretraining to reinforcement learning and agentic workloads. We run Slurm and Kubernetes at large scale. Our scheduling is coordinated and topology-sensitive on rack-scale systems. We manage fair sharing and quotas for hundreds of research teams. We support preemption and reservations. Elastic jobs recover from failure without losing progress. You will own real parts of the scheduling stack, and the opportunity to ship code into our open-source and internal platform code, and see the result in GPU-hours returned to researchers within days. The researchers training NVIDIA's own models are your users, and they will tell you quickly what works.

What You'll Be Doing

Design and build scheduling for large GPU fleets on both Slurm and Kubernetes. That covers queueing, gang and topology-aware placement on rack-scale NVLink systems, preemption, reservations and backfill that reaches the end of very deep queues.
Build the policy layer: fair share, quotas and allocations across many research teams, driven from a central allocation system and enforced the same way on every scheduler.
Run Slurm as a cloud-native service on Kubernetes, and extend Kubernetes batch scheduling (Kueue and its ecosystem) for training, reinforcement learning, sandboxes and inference.
Build services around the scheduler: reservation automation, node-health-aware placement, workflow orchestration across clusters, and APIs that let other platforms submit and track work.
Measure and raise goodput: GPU occupancy, waste, fairness and time to start for large jobs. Use the data to choose what to build next.
Own reliability for the components you build: on-call, incident analysis and fixes that remove whole classes of failure, so problems are found before researchers hit them.
Work upstream and across teams: contribute to Slurm, Kubernetes and related open-source projects, and partner with platform, storage, networking and research teams.

What We Need To See

BS or MS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience.
6+ years building production systems software.
Deep experience with at least one batch or cluster scheduler, such as Slurm, Kueue, Volcano, KAI, YuniKorn or a scheduler you built. You should be able to explain its internals, not only its configuration.
Strong programming in Go, C or C++, plus Python for tooling and analysis.
Hands-on Kubernetes experience: controllers or operators, CRDs, scheduling and resource management.
Solid Linux systems knowledge: containers (Docker, Podman, Enroot or Apptainer), cgroups, networking basics and debugging under load.
A track record of owning a service in production and making it measurably better.
Clear written and spoken communication with engineers and researchers.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Experience scheduling large-scale AI training: thousands of GPUs, NVLink and InfiniBand or RoCE topology, multi-node jobs that must start together.
Contributions to Slurm, Kubernetes SIG Scheduling, Kueue, Volcano, KAI or similar open-source schedulers.
Experience running Slurm on Kubernetes (Slinky or similar), or building Kubernetes operators for batch or HPC workloads.
Familiarity with RL, agentic or inference workloads and what they need from a scheduler: heterogeneous jobs, sandboxes, elastic scale and fast restarts.
Experience with workflow orchestrators such as Flyte, Airflow, Ray or Kubeflow at scale.

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are:

184,000 USD – 287,500 USD for Level 4; and 224,000 USD – 356,500 USD for Level 5.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 14, 2026.
